verdict: Evergy's hot summer and growing roster of giant data-center customers lifted revenue 16% and profit 29%, and management raised its full-year guidance.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP, diluted)
kpis.note: Adjusted EPS $2.58; vs $2.03 a year ago

segments.name: Residential
segments.note: Homes in Kansas and Missouri — warmer weather meant more electricity used and sold.

segments.name: Commercial
segments.note: Businesses buying electricity across Evergy's Kansas and Missouri territories.

segments.name: Transmission
segments.note: Fees for moving power across Evergy's high-voltage network for others.

segments.name: Wholesale
segments.note: Power sold into wholesale markets beyond Evergy's own customers.

segments.name: Other & non-contract revenue
segments.note: Other retail and miscellaneous contract revenue ($24M) plus $70M of revenue not from customer contracts, such as regulatory alternative-revenue programs.

opex.name: Operation & maintenance
opex.note: Running and repairing plants, lines and customer operations day to day.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of generation and grid assets over their long lives — rising as Evergy invests.

opex.name: Taxes other than income taxes
opex.note: Mostly property taxes on plants and networks in Kansas and Missouri.

otherDetail: Other income of $20M, less $168M of interest expense, for net other expense of $148M; plus $3M of equity earnings from part-owned investees, which Evergy reports after tax. Net income in the flow is the consolidated $616M; $613M was attributable to Evergy after $3M for noncontrolling interests, matching the $2.59 diluted EPS.

takeaways.title: Adjusted EPS up 27%
takeaways.text: Adjusted earnings were $610M, or $2.58 a share, up from $475M and $2.03 a year ago — warmer weather, growth in demand, large-customer revenue and recovery of regulated investments all helped.

takeaways.title: Data centers keep coming
takeaways.text: Evergy signed amendments adding about 250 MW to existing large-customer service agreements, plus a letter of intent with Digital Realty for a 1.4 GW expansion next to an existing 600 MW project.

takeaways.title: Guidance raised, dividend up 4%
takeaways.text: Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance rose to $4.35–$4.50, and the quarterly dividend increased 4% to $0.7225 a share ($2.89 annualized). Long-term adjusted EPS growth of 6–8%+ through 2030 was reaffirmed.

oneTimers: Adjusted earnings strip out a $5M gain from a transmission-revenue-requirement settlement and $1M of losses on early-stage clean-energy investments (plus their tax effects) — which is why adjusted profit of $610M sits slightly below the $613M GAAP figure (both attributable).
footerNote: Utility layout: fuel and purchased power ($473M) plus SPP network transmission costs ($124M) are treated as the cost of revenue; the remaining operating lines mirror Evergy's income statement in its Q3 2026 Form 10-Q. Segment revenues are Evergy's revenue-from-contracts by customer class (10-Q), with non-contract revenue grouped into Other. The earnings release itself (Ex. 99.1) carries the headline results and guidance; the full statements are in the 10-Q.
